flip.title: Flip assumptions
flip.note: Loan principal is repaid from equity, not charged twice as an expense. Carrying expense includes modeled loan interest and property tax; other ongoing flip costs are not modeled.

report.title: Property ROI - chosen assumptions and modeled results
report.sale_cash: Sale proceeds after selling costs and loan payoff
report.annual_cash: Cash flow after modeled debt payments (year 1)
report.illustrative: Illustrative estimates from the chosen inputs, not guaranteed returns or a property valuation.
report.currency_note: All amounts are USD. No foreign-exchange conversion is applied. Detailed report amounts are rounded to cents; screen summaries may be abbreviated.
report.costs: Initial cash invested is the cash purchase price or financed down payment, plus entered acquisition closing costs and renovation/furnishing. For an all-cash purchase, the entire purchase price is required. Closing costs are separate from the down payment.
report.rental_definition: Cash-on-cash return is year-one cash flow after modeled debt payments divided by initial cash invested. Gross yield is effective gross rental income divided by purchase price; cap rate is NOI divided by purchase price. A zero initial investment has no defined cash-on-cash return. Management fees follow projected rental income; fixed maintenance, insurance and tax assumptions use the initial purchase price. Debt payments stop at the entered term. The ten-year cash-flow-plus-value-change metric excludes sale costs and equity from principal paydown; it is not a total-return or IRR calculation. The ten-year measure adds modeled net cash flows and appreciation gain. It does not subtract upfront closing/works or exit costs, or add equity from principal paydown. It is not total profit, total ROI or IRR. Simple payback is initial cash divided by positive year-one cash flow, assuming that flow remains constant. It does not use rent growth, appreciation or later debt-payment changes. It is undefined with zero initial cash or non-positive year-one cash flow.
report.flip_definition: Flip profit equals modeled resale less purchase price, acquisition closing costs, renovation, selling costs, loan interest during the hold and modeled property tax. Principal repayment is not expensed twice. The equivalent check is sale cash after the remaining loan payoff, less initial cash invested and holding cash outflows. Flip percentage return uses initial cash invested and is not annualized.
report.exemption_note: The default exemption is zero. Enter only remaining approved years for this investment; eligibility is not verified here. Law 195-13, Article 9 amending Article 7 of Law 158-01, links a qualifying project's 15-year period to project completion, not each purchase. The annual tax-budget percentage is not statutory IPI: DGII bases IPI on taxable assessed wealth, with owner-specific rules and exemptions. No peso threshold or currency conversion is inferred.
report.unmodeled: No loan origination points, prepayment penalties, currency changes, income or capital-gains taxes, insurance changes, sale taxes, utilities, reserves or other unentered charges are invented. For flips, rental income, management, maintenance and insurance are not included as ongoing holding items. Obtain the actual costs and professional review before making a decision.
report.link_note: The restore link contains only the calculator's numeric assumptions, scenario, financing choice, currency and language. Anyone with the link can view those inputs; no personal/contact information is included.
report.ten_year_note: The ten-year measure adds modeled net cash flows and appreciation gain. It does not subtract upfront closing/works or exit costs, or add equity from principal paydown. It is not total profit, total ROI or IRR.
